title: Sharing my repo for making animations like this
author: LatentBlade
selftext:
[https://gitlab.com/drnknmstrr/spritesheet\_example](https://gitlab.com/drnknmstrr/spritesheet_example)

  
Yes, my first frame is wrong. This was true first run output of this notebook (with some clean up in Krita). If people have questions please ask them here. If there is interest I can work on this more and share more details. I'm finding this workflow to take a lot of work and I'm hoping to figure out something simpler.

comments.body: Such a high detail sprite needs way more frames, thanks for the share though

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: That's literally what the read me says 😂

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: I was tired of everyone posting thinly veiled ads or not describing their workflows so I thought I'd at least share what I have

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: I added more frames and now people tell me I have too many 😂

comments.author: Southern_Charge5794
comments.body:
I spent hours for trying to create perfect animations and read a lot of posts about how people obsessed with Nano Banana and GPT-Image-2. To be honest results that I gave with nano banana are maybe acceptable for low-res bitmap and for anything else it is very inconsistent and animation became not so smooth. Haven't seen nothing better than Kling O3 loop animations. For example here is 24 fps animation where I generated 3 sec video -> extracted 24 frames -> removed background for every frame to make it transparent. I do like results, the next step is to process stunning VFXs by fixing transparency issue

https://i.redd.it/9hy1xyfx7zzg1.gif

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: Wow that looks really good!  I'll have to try kling out. Thanks!

replies.author: Southern_Charge5794
replies.body: I find it great for any animations, but especially for loops. Try any image-to-video model, they have pretty good quality and some can generate in 4k

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: It's actually compatible with the workflow I posted here. I'm taking frames and generating the in between video. The downside is it adds too much but I probably can pull out just what I need

replies.author: Southern_Charge5794
replies.body: According to your repo you do generate animations frame by frame that at least suboptimal. You can generate sprite sheet directly up to 4k and this is a lot of frames. I even tried to create more than one animation with this approach. Like I said this maybe is ok for some animations but results can't be smooth

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: I found I've had more control going frame by frame. It lets me generate multiple versions of each frame to mix and match the best ones. Whenever I asked for a sprite sheet it get the proportions of the frames all messed up which is harder to fix for me than centering each frame manually. Again, I'm nit saying this is optimal. Just sharing so we can compare notes.

replies.author: SucculentSpine
replies.body: Is this a particular model type for looping animations? Or are you just specifying an action between the same start and end images?

replies.author: Southern_Charge5794
replies.body: Oh, there are start and end frame options. I am writing something dog scratches his head with one paw as if you didn't specify that it will do with both simultaneously)
